Concept note draft · Design hypothesis

System 1, System 2, and embodied agents

The useful question is what fast execution and slower diagnosis need to tell each other.

My thesis uses perception, cognition and response to locate difficulties in human–robot interaction. Those are processing functions. A fast/slow distinction asks a different question: how much deliberation does the system allocate, and when?

The two descriptions should not be treated as a one-to-one mapping. Perception can involve deliberate reinspection. A plan can be familiar and quickly retrieved. An action can require careful online correction. An end-to-end model can also fuse these functions without exposing separate modules.

A proposed interface

For an embodied agent, I would begin by making the information crossing between execution and diagnosis explicit.

Execution reportsDiagnosis returns
Observation and estimated stateAlternative explanations to test
Expected versus observed outcomeA discriminating intervention
Action, timing and constraint violationsSuccess criteria and a stopping rule
Missing evidence or ambiguous stateWhat additional observation to request

These records should refer to inspectable observations. A plausible narrative about a failure is a hypothesis until a test supports it.

A small example

Suppose a robot fails to pick up a chess piece. A board-localisation error, an incorrect piece estimate and a grasp-execution problem could produce a similar final outcome. Repeating the full task may provide little new information.

A better next experiment might acquire another view, verify the board transform, or test the grasp at a known position. The useful behaviour is the choice of intervention that separates candidate explanations.

How I would test it

I would compare a single controller with an explicit executor–diagnoser arrangement, keeping the underlying model, available evidence and total budget fixed. The evaluation would include diagnosis accuracy against controlled faults, unnecessary interventions, task recovery and cost.

This is a later experiment. First I want a reproducible scientific-agent loop and a trustworthy evaluator. Adding fast and slow components before establishing those would make the source of any improvement harder to identify.

Status: an architectural hypothesis inspired by the thesis framework, not a finding about machine cognition or evidence that a robot should reproduce human cognitive architecture.

Source grounding: supplied thesis Chapter 1 (processing stages and modalities) and Chapter 6, Section 6.4 (limits of modular stage descriptions).
